claim_being_audited: Whether the current release can be certified as compliant on the basis of aggregate readiness while a material health-plan benefits support regression exists, given the policy requirement that current release documentation disclose material segment weaknesses unless they are resolved or covered by approved mitigation.
specific_concerns: No admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation actually discloses the health-plan benefits support weakness.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance covering the subgroup regression before launch.
The actor's certification theory depends on a condition that is not evidenced in the record: current-release disclosure of the material limitation.
Prior approval from nine weeks earlier is explicitly stale relative to the current corpus refresh and eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
The informal monitoring note is not equivalent to reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure under the stated policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant rather than only potentially defensible if current release documentation contains the required disclosure.
Any implication that aggregate readiness plus public governance principles is sufficient by itself to satisfy the release policy.
Any reliance on the informal post-launch monitoring comment as if it were approved mitigation or risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or release documentation showing explicit disclosure of the health-plan benefits support limitation.
Provide any approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance artifact covering the subgroup regression before launch.
Provide the current-release certification packet section that maps the disclosed weakness to the policy requirement for material limitations.
decision_criteria: Policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results.
Policy requires material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation before launch.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal support deployment readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure/mitigation predicate.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring comments may provide context but cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.

My verdict would change to compliant_with_caveats or compliant if admissible evidence showed the current release documentation already discloses the subgroup weakness, or if an approved mitigation/risk acceptance artifact exists and covers it.
